text:
Wyatt Johnston spent the first month of the season getting chances and not scoring. Now the goals are arriving: one in each of his last four games, including one in Vegas off a lucky bounce to the back door that cut the deficit to 3-2 with 1:18 left.

That run was overdue. He still has only 7 goals on 10.7 expected goals, and his 1.64 individual expected goals per 60 is an elite rate of getting to dangerous ice. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking agreed last season: 93rd percentile for chances from in front of the net. Evolving-Hockey had the same story for 2025-26, 2.5 expected wins against 0.9 actual.

The less flattering part is the 5v5 share. Dallas is right at 50% of the chances with him on the ice, slightly worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey flagged his defensive cost last year. Eleven of his 20 points have come on the power play. If the finishing catches up to the looks, our range has him at 25 to 40 goals for the season.
